nodes.title: Morphism schemes gives representable transformation
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02W9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02W9}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$ and let
$X$, $Y$ be objects of $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Then
$$
h_f : h_X \longrightarrow h_Y
$$
is a representable transformation of functors.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem morphismScheme_representable {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    [HasPullbacks C] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    RepresentableTransformation C (morphismScheme f) := by
  exact Functor.relativelyRepresentable.map yoneda f

@[simp]

nodes.title: Composition representable transformations
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WA}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G, H : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $a : F \to G$, $b : G \to H$ be representable transformations of functors.
Then
$$
b \circ a : F \longrightarrow H
$$
is a representable transformation of functors.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem representableTransformation_comp {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {F G H : Presheaf C} (a : F ⟶ G) (b : G ⟶ H)
    (ha : RepresentableTransformation C a)
    (hb : RepresentableTransformation C b) :
    RepresentableTransformation C (a ≫ b) := by
  exact MorphismProperty.comp_mem (RepresentableTransformation C) a b ha hb

nodes.title: Base change representable transformations
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WB}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WB}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G, H : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $a : F \to G$ be a representable transformation of functors.
Let $b : H \to G$ be any transformation of functors.
Consider the fibre product diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}H \times_{b, G, a} F \underset{b'}{\longrightarrow}\underset{a'}{\downarrow} & F \overset{a}{\downarrow} \\ H \overset{b}{\longrightarrow} & G\end{array}
$$
Then the base change $a'$ is a representable transformation of functors.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem representableTransformation_baseChange {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {F G H K : Presheaf C} {a : F ⟶ G} {b : H ⟶ G}
    {a' : K ⟶ H} {p : K ⟶ F}
    (sq : IsPullback p a' a b)
    (ha : RepresentableTransformation C a) :
    RepresentableTransformation C a' := by
  exact MorphismProperty.IsStableUnderBaseChange.of_isPullback sq ha

nodes.title: Product representable transformations
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WC}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F_i, G_i : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$, $i = 1, 2$.
Let $a_i : F_i \to G_i$, $i = 1, 2$
be representable transformations of functors.
Then
$$
a_1 \times a_2 : F_1 \times F_2 \longrightarrow G_1 \times G_2
$$
is a representable transformation of functors.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem representableTransformation_prod
    {F₁ G₁ F₂ G₂ : Presheaf C}
    (f₁ : F₁ ⟶ G₁) (f₂ : F₂ ⟶ G₂)
    (h₁ : RepresentableTransformation C f₁)
    (h₂ : RepresentableTransformation C f₂) :
    RepresentableTransformation C (prod.map f₁ f₂) := by
  have hleft : RepresentableTransformation C (prod.map f₁ (𝟙 F₂)) :=
    representableTransformation_baseChange
      (IsPullback.of_prod_fst_with_id f₁ F₂) h₁
  have hright : RepresentableTransformation C (prod.map (𝟙 G₁) f₂) :=
    representableTransformation_baseChange
      (isPullback_prod_snd_with_id f₂ G₁) h₂
  have hcomp : RepresentableTransformation C
      (prod.map f₁ (𝟙 F₂) ≫ prod.map (𝟙 G₁) f₂) :=
    representableTransformation_comp _ _ hleft hright
  rw [prod.map_map] at hcomp
  simpa using hcomp

end PresheafProducts

nodes.title: Representable transformation to sheaf
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WD}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $a : F \to G$ be a representable transformation of functors.
If $G$ is a sheaf, then so is $F$.

nodes.title: Representable transformation diagonal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05L9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 05L9}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $a : F \to G$ be a representable transformation of functors.
Then $\Delta_{F/G} : F \to F \times_G F$ is representable.

nodes.title: Relative representable property
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/025V}{\texttt{Stacks tag 025V}}


With $S$, and $a : F \to G$ representable as above.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms of schemes which
\begin{enumerate}
\item is preserved under any base change,
see Schemes, Definition \ref{schemes-definition-preserved-by-base-change},
and
\item is fppf local on the base, see
Descent, Definition \ref{descent-definition-property-morphisms-local}.
\end{enumerate}
In this case we say that $a$ has {\it property $\mathcal{P}$} if for every
$U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$ and
any $\xi \in G(U)$ the resulting morphism of schemes
$V_\xi \to U$ has property $\mathcal{P}$.
nodes.lean_source:
abbrev RelativeMorphismProperty {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D] (F : C ⥤ D) (P : MorphismProperty C) :
    MorphismProperty D :=
  P.relative F

nodes.title: Morphism schemes gives representable transformation property
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WJ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WJ}}



Let $S$, $X$, $Y$ be objects of $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be as in
Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}.
Then $h_X \longrightarrow h_Y$ has property $\mathcal{P}$ if
and only if $f$ has property $\mathcal{P}$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem morphismScheme_property_iff {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    [HasPullbacks C] (P : MorphismProperty C)
    [P.IsStableUnderBaseChange] {X Y : C} (f : X ⟶ Y) :
    PresheafMorphismProperty P (morphismScheme f) ↔ P f := by
  exact MorphismProperty.relative_map_iff

nodes.title: Composition representable transformations property
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WK}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WK}}



Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G, H : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property as in
Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}
which is stable under composition.
Let $a : F \to G$, $b : G \to H$ be representable transformations of functors.
If $a$ and $b$ have property $\mathcal{P}$ so does
$b \circ a : F \longrightarrow H$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem relativeMorphismProperty_comp {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D] {F : C ⥤ D} {P : MorphismProperty C}
    [F.Faithful] [F.Full] [P.IsStableUnderComposition]
    {X Y Z : D} {f : X ⟶ Y} {g : Y ⟶ Z}
    (hf : RelativeMorphismProperty F P f)
    (hg : RelativeMorphismProperty F P g) :
    RelativeMorphismProperty F P (f ≫ g) := by
  exact MorphismProperty.comp_mem (RelativeMorphismProperty F P) f g hf hg

nodes.title: Base change representable transformations property
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WL}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WL}}



Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G, H : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property as in
Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}.
Let $a : F \to G$ be a representable transformation of functors.
Let $b : H \to G$ be any transformation of functors.
Consider the fibre product diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}H \times_{b, G, a} F \underset{b'}{\longrightarrow}\underset{a'}{\downarrow} & F \overset{a}{\downarrow} \\ H \overset{b}{\longrightarrow} & G\end{array}
$$
If $a$ has property $\mathcal{P}$ then also the base change $a'$
has property $\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.title: Descent representable transformations property
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03KD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03KD}}



Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G, H : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property as in
Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}.
Let $a : F \to G$ be a representable transformation of functors.
Let $b : H \to G$ be any transformation of functors.
Consider the fibre product diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}H \times_{b, G, a} F \underset{b'}{\longrightarrow}\underset{a'}{\downarrow} & F \overset{a}{\downarrow} \\ H \overset{b}{\longrightarrow} & G\end{array}
$$
Assume that $b$ induces a surjective map of fppf sheaves $H^\# \to G^\#$.
In this case, if $a'$ has property $\mathcal{P}$, then also $a$
has property $\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.title: Product representable transformations property
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WM}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WM}}



Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F_i, G_i : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$,
$i = 1, 2$.
Let $a_i : F_i \to G_i$, $i = 1, 2$ be representable transformations
of functors.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property as in
Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}
which is stable under composition.
If $a_1$ and $a_2$ have property $\mathcal{P}$ so does
$a_1 \times a_2 : F_1 \times F_2 \longrightarrow G_1 \times G_2$.

nodes.title: Representable transformations property implication
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YO}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02YO}}



Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $a : F \to G$ be a representable transformation of functors.
Let $\mathcal{P}$, $\mathcal{P}'$ be properties as in
Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}.
Suppose that for any morphism of schemes $f : X \to Y$
we have $\mathcal{P}(f) \Rightarrow \mathcal{P}'(f)$.
If $a$ has property $\mathcal{P}$ then
$a$ has property $\mathcal{P}'$.
nodes.lean_source:
theorem relativeMorphismProperty_mono {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D] {F : C ⥤ D}
    {P P' : MorphismProperty C} (h : P ≤ P') :
    RelativeMorphismProperty F P ≤ RelativeMorphismProperty F P' :=
  MorphismProperty.relative_monotone h

nodes.title: Surjective flat locally finite presentation
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05VM}{\texttt{Stacks tag 05VM}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be sheaves.
Let $a : F \to G$ be representable, flat,
locally of finite presentation, and surjective.
Then $a : F \to G$ is surjective as a map of sheaves.

nodes.title: Representable diagonal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/025W}{\texttt{Stacks tag 025W}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$ be a presheaf of sets on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the diagonal $F \to F \times F$ is representable,
\item for $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$ and any $a \in F(U)$
the map $a : h_U \to F$ is representable,
\item for every pair $U, V \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$
and any $a \in F(U)$, $b \in F(V)$ the fibre product
$h_U \times_{a, F, b} h_V$ is representable.
\end{enumerate}
nodes.lean_source:
theorem relativeRepresentable_diag_iff_pairwise {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D] {F : C ⥤ D} {X : D}
    [HasBinaryProducts C] [HasPullbacks C]
    [HasPullbacks D] [HasBinaryProducts D] [HasTerminal D]
    [F.Full] [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) F]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan F] :
    RelativeRepresentable F (Limits.diag X) ↔
      ∀ ⦃a b : C⦄ (g : F.obj a ⟶ X) (h : F.obj b ⟶ X),
        ∃ (c : C) (p : c ⟶ a) (q : c ⟶ b),
          IsPullback (F.map p) (F.map q) g h := by
  rw [relativeRepresentable_diag_iff]
  constructor
  · intro hdiag a b g h
    obtain ⟨c, q, fst, sq⟩ := hdiag g h
    refine ⟨c, F.preimage fst, q, ?_⟩
    simpa only [Functor.map_preimage] using sq
  · intro hdiag a g b h
    obtain ⟨c, p, q, sq⟩ := hdiag g h
    exact ⟨c, q, F.map p, sq⟩

theorem relativeRepresentable_diag_iff {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C]
    {D : Type u'} [Category.{v'} D] {F : C ⥤ D} {X : D}
    [HasBinaryProducts C] [HasPullbacks C]
    [HasPullbacks D] [HasBinaryProducts D] [HasTerminal D]
    [F.Full] [PreservesLimitsOfShape (Discrete WalkingPair) F]
    [PreservesLimitsOfShape WalkingCospan F] :
    RelativeRepresentable F (Limits.diag X) ↔
      ∀ ⦃a : C⦄ (g : F.obj a ⟶ X), RelativeRepresentable F g :=
  Functor.relativelyRepresentable.diag_iff

nodes.title: Transformation diagonal properties
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0CB7}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0CB7}}



Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$ be a presheaf of sets on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property as in
Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}.
If for every $U, V \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$ and $a \in F(U)$,
$b \in F(V)$ we have
\begin{enumerate}
\item $h_U \times_{a, F, b} h_V$ is representable, say by the scheme $W$, and
\item the morphism $W \to U \times_S V$ corresponding to
$h_U \times_{a, F, b} h_V \to h_U \times h_V$ has property $\mathcal{P}$,
\end{enumerate}
then $\Delta : F \to F \times F$ is representable and has
property $\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.title: Algebraic space
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/025Y}{\texttt{Stacks tag 025Y}}



Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
An {\it algebraic space over $S$} is a presheaf
$$
F : (\Sch/S)^{opp}_{fppf} \longrightarrow \textit{Sets}
$$
with the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item The presheaf $F$ is a sheaf.
\item The diagonal morphism $F  \to F \times F$ is representable.
\item There exists a scheme $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$
and a map $h_U \to F$ which is surjective and \'etale\footnote{See
Lemma \ref{spaces-lemma-representable-diagonal},
Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}, and
Remark \ref{spaces-remark-warning}.}.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Scheme is space
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/025Z}{\texttt{Stacks tag 025Z}}


A scheme is an algebraic space. More precisely,
given a scheme $T \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$
the representable functor $h_T$ is an algebraic space.

nodes.title: Morphism algebraic spaces
Product spaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02X0}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02X0}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G$ be algebraic spaces over $S$.
Then $F \times G$ is an algebraic space, and is a product
in the category of algebraic spaces over $S$.

nodes.title: Fibre product spaces over sheaf with representable diagonal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04T9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 04T9}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $H$ be a sheaf on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ whose diagonal
is representable. Let $F, G$ be algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $F \to H$, $G \to H$ be maps of sheaves.
Then $F \times_H G$ is an algebraic space.

nodes.title: Fibre product spaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02X2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02X2}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F \to H$, $G \to H$ be morphisms of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Then $F \times_H G$ is an algebraic space, and is a fibre product
in the category of algebraic spaces over $S$.

nodes.title: Coproduct sheaves open and closed
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0F15}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0F15}}


Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$. Let $F$ and $G$ be sheaves on
$(\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp}$ and denote $F \amalg G$ the coproduct
in the category of sheaves. The map $F \to F \amalg G$ is representable by
open and closed immersions.

nodes.title: Representable sheaf coproduct sheaves
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WO}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WO}}


Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$.
Let $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$.
Given a set $I$ and sheaves $F_i$ on $\Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$,
if $U \cong \coprod_{i\in I} F_i$
as sheaves, then each $F_i$ is representable by an open and closed
subscheme $U_i$ and $U \cong \coprod U_i$ as schemes.

nodes.title: Algebraic space coproduct sheaves
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WP}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WP}}


Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$.
Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Given a set $I$ and sheaves $F_i$ on
$\Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$,
if $F \cong \coprod_{i\in I} F_i$ as sheaves,
then each $F_i$ is an algebraic space over $S$.

nodes.title: Coproduct algebraic spaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WQ}}


Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$.
Suppose given a set $I$ and algebraic spaces $F_i$, $i \in I$.
Then $F = \coprod_{i \in I} F_i$ is an algebraic space
provided $I$, and the $F_i$ are not too ``large'': for example if we
can choose surjective \'etale morphisms $U_i \to F_i$ such that
$\coprod_{i \in I} U_i$ is isomorphic to an object of
$(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$, then $F$ is an algebraic space.

nodes.title: Glueing algebraic spaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WR}}



Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$.
Let $F$ be a presheaf of sets on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $F$ is a sheaf,
\item there exists an index set $I$
and subfunctors $F_i \subset F$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item each $F_i$ is an algebraic space,
\item each $F_i \to F$ is representable,
\item each $F_i \to F$ is an open immersion (see
Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}),
\item the map $\coprod F_i \to F$ is surjective as a map of sheaves, and
\item $\coprod F_i$ is an algebraic space (set theoretic condition, see
Lemma \ref{spaces-lemma-coproduct-algebraic-spaces}).
\end{enumerate}
\end{enumerate}
Then $F$ is an algebraic space.

nodes.title: Space presentation
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0262}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0262}}


Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$. Let $f : U \to F$ be a
surjective \'etale morphism from a scheme to $F$. Set $R = U \times_F U$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $j : R \to U \times_S U$ defines an equivalence relation on
$U$ over $S$ (see
Groupoids, Definition \ref{groupoids-definition-equivalence-relation}).
\item the morphisms $s, t : R \to U$ are \'etale, and
\item the diagram
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}R \longrightarrow\longrightarrow & U \longrightarrow & F\end{array}
$$
is a coequalizer diagram in $\Sh((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Etale equivalence relation
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WS}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WS}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $U$ be a scheme over $S$.
An {\it \'etale equivalence relation} on $U$ over $S$
is an equivalence relation $j : R \to U \times_S U$
such that $s, t : R \to U$ are \'etale morphisms of schemes.

nodes.title: Presentation
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0263}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0263}}


Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
A {\it presentation} of $F$ is given by a scheme
$U$ over $S$ and an \'etale equivalence relation $R$ on $U$ over $S$, and
a surjective \'etale morphism $U \to F$ such that $R = U \times_F U$.

nodes.title: Pullback etale equivalence relation
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WT}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $U$ be a scheme over $S$.
Let $j = (s, t) : R \to U \times_S U$
be an \'etale equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$.
Let $U' \to U$ be an \'etale morphism.
Let $R'$ be the restriction of $R$ to $U'$, see
Groupoids, Definition \ref{groupoids-definition-restrict-relation}.
Then $j' : R' \to U' \times_S U'$ is an \'etale equivalence
relation also.

nodes.title: Finding opens
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WU}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WU}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $U$ be a scheme over $S$.
Let $j = (s, t) : R \to U \times_S U$ be a pre-relation.
Let $g : U' \to U$ be a morphism.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $j$ is an equivalence relation,
\item $s, t : R \to U$ are surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation,
\item $g$ is flat and locally of finite presentation.
\end{enumerate}
Let $R' = R|_{U'}$ be the restriction of $R$ to $U'$. Then
$U'/R' \to U/R$ is representable, and is an open immersion.

nodes.title: When it works it works
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WV}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $U$ be a scheme over $S$.
Let $j = (s, t) : R \to U \times_S U$
be an \'etale equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$.
If the quotient $U/R$ is an algebraic space, then
$U \to U/R$ is \'etale and surjective. Hence
$(U, R, U \to U/R)$ is a presentation of the algebraic
space $U/R$.

nodes.title: Presentation quasi compact
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0265}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0265}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $U$ be a scheme over $S$.
Let $j = (s, t) : R \to U \times_S U$
be an \'etale equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$.
Assume that $U$ is affine. Then the quotient $F = U/R$
is an algebraic space, and $U \to F$ is \'etale and surjective.

nodes.title: Presentation
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WW}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $U$ be a scheme over $S$.
Let $j = (s, t) : R \to U \times_S U$
be an \'etale equivalence relation on $U$ over $S$.
Then the quotient $U/R$ is an algebraic space,
and $U \to U/R$ is \'etale and surjective, in other words
$(U, R, U \to U/R)$ is a presentation of $U/R$.

nodes.title: Etale locally representable gives space
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BGQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BGQ}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$ be a sheaf on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$
such that there exists $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$ and a map
$U \to F$ which is representable, surjective, and \'etale.
Then $F$ is an algebraic space.

nodes.title: Etale locally representable by space gives space
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BGR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BGR}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$. Let $G$ be an algebraic
space over $S$, let $F$ be a sheaf on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$, and let
$G \to F$ be a representable transformation of functors which is
surjective and \'etale. Then $F$ is an algebraic space.

nodes.title: A functor that admits a representable morphism to an algebraic space is an algebraic sp...
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WY}}



Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $G \to F$ be a representable transformation of functors.
Then $G$ is an algebraic space.

nodes.title: Representable morphisms spaces property
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02WZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02WZ}}



Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$, $G$ be algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $G \to F$ be a representable morphism.
Let $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$, and $q : U \to F$
surjective and \'etale. Set $V = G \times_F U$.
Finally, let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms
of schemes as in Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}.
Then $G \to F$ has property $\mathcal{P}$ if and only if
$V \to U$ has property $\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.title: Morphism sheaves with P effective descent etale
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03I2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03I2}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $G \to F$ be a transformation of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms of schemes.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\mathcal{P}$ is preserved under any base change, fppf local on the
base, and morphisms of type $\mathcal{P}$ satisfy descent for fppf coverings,
see Descent, Definition \ref{descent-definition-descending-types-morphisms},
\item $G$ is a sheaf,
\item $F$ is an algebraic space,
\item there exists a $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$
and a surjective \'etale morphism $U \to F$ such that
$V = G \times_F U$ is representable, and
\item $V \to U$ has $\mathcal{P}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then $G$ is an algebraic space, $G \to F$ is representable and has property
$\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.title: Lift morphism presentations
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02X1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02X1}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G$ be algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $a : F \to G$ be a morphism.
Given any $V \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$
and a surjective \'etale morphism $q : V \to G$ there exists
a $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$
and a commutative diagram
$$
\begin{array}{cc}U \underset{p}{\downarrow}\underset{\alpha}{\longrightarrow} & V \overset{q}{\downarrow} \\ F \overset{a}{\longrightarrow} & G\end{array}
$$
with $p$ surjective and \'etale.

nodes.title: Immersion
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YU}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02YU}}



Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$ be a scheme.
Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$
is called an {\it open immersion} if it is representable, and an open immersion
in the sense of Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}.
\item An {\it open subspace} of $F$ is a subfunctor $F' \subset F$
such that $F'$ is an algebraic space and $F' \to F$ is an
open immersion.
\item A morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$
is called a {\it closed immersion} if it is representable, and a closed
immersion in the sense of
Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}.
\item A {\it closed subspace} of $F$ is a subfunctor $F' \subset F$
such that $F'$ is an algebraic space and $F' \to F$ is a
closed immersion.
\item A morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$
is called an {\it immersion} if it is representable, and an immersion
in the sense of Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}.
\item A {\it locally closed subspace} of $F$ is a subfunctor $F' \subset F$
such that $F'$ is an algebraic space and $F' \to F$ is an
immersion.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Composition immersions
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02YV}}


Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$ be a scheme.
A composition of (closed, resp.\ open) immersions of
algebraic spaces over $S$ is a (closed, resp.\ open)
immersion of algebraic spaces over $S$.

nodes.title: Base change immersions
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02YW}}


Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$ be a scheme.
A base change of a (closed, resp.\ open) immersion
of algebraic spaces over $S$ is a (closed, resp.\ open)
immersion of algebraic spaces over $S$.

nodes.title: Sub subspaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02YX}}


Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$ be a scheme.
Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$. Let $F_1$, $F_2$ be
locally closed subspaces of $F$. If $F_1 \subset F_2$ as subfunctors
of $F$, then $F_1$ is a locally closed subspace of $F_2$.
Similarly for closed and open subspaces.

nodes.title: Zariski open covering
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02YY}}


Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$ be a scheme.
Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
A {\it Zariski covering} $\{F_i \subset F\}_{i \in I}$ of $F$
is given by a set $I$ and a collection of open subspaces
$F_i \subset F$ such that $\coprod F_i \to F$ is a surjective
map of sheaves.

nodes.title: Small Zariski site
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02YZ}}


Let $S \in \Ob(\Sch_{fppf})$ be a scheme. Let $F$ be an algebraic space over
$S$. A {\it small Zariski site $F_{Zar}$} of an algebraic space $F$ is one
of the sites described above.

nodes.title: Properties diagonal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02X4}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02X4}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\Delta : F \to F \times F$ be the diagonal morphism.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Delta$ is locally of finite type,
\item $\Delta$ is a monomorphism,
\item $\Delta$ is separated, and
\item $\Delta$ is locally quasi-finite.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Separated
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02X5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02X5}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\Delta : F \to F \times F$ be the diagonal morphism.
\begin{enumerate}
\item We say $F$ is {\it separated over $S$} if $\Delta$ is a closed immersion.
\item We say $F$ is {\it locally separated over $S$}\footnote{In the
literature this often refers to quasi-separated and
locally separated algebraic spaces.} if $\Delta$ is an
immersion.
\item We say $F$ is {\it quasi-separated over $S$} if $\Delta$ is quasi-compact.
\item We say $F$ is {\it Zariski locally quasi-separated over $S$}\footnote{This
definition was suggested by B.\ Conrad.} if there
exists a Zariski covering $F = \bigcup_{i \in I} F_i$ such that
each $F_i$ is quasi-separated.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Quotient
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02Z2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02Z2}}



Let $U \to S$ be a morphism of $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $G$ be an abstract group. Let $G \to \text{Aut}_S(U)$
be a group homomorphism. Assume
\begin{itemize}
\item[(*)] if $u \in U$ is a point, and $g(u) = u$
for some non-identity element $g \in G$, then $g$
induces a nontrivial automorphism of $\kappa(u)$.
\end{itemize}
Then
$$
j :
R = \coprod\nolimits_{g \in G} U
\longrightarrow
U \times_S U,
\quad
(g, x) \longmapsto (g(x), x)
$$
is an \'etale equivalence relation and hence
$$
F = U/R
$$
is an algebraic space by Theorem \ref{spaces-theorem-presentation}.

nodes.title: Quotient
Quotient finite separated
Quotient field map
Change big site
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03FP}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03FP}}


Suppose given big sites $\Sch_{fppf}$ and $\Sch'_{fppf}$.
Assume that $\Sch_{fppf}$ is contained in $\Sch'_{fppf}$,
see Topologies, Section \ref{topologies-section-change-alpha}.
Let $S$ be an object of $\Sch_{fppf}$. Let
\begin{align*}
g : \Sh((\Sch/S)_{fppf})
\longrightarrow
\Sh((\Sch'/S)_{fppf}), \\
f : \Sh((\Sch'/S)_{fppf})
\longrightarrow
\Sh((\Sch/S)_{fppf})
\end{align*}
be the morphisms of topoi of
Topologies, Lemma \ref{topologies-lemma-change-alpha}.
Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $F$ is representable by a scheme
$X \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$ over $S$,
then $f^{-1}F$ is representable too, in fact it is representable by the
same scheme $X$, now viewed as an object of $(\Sch'/S)_{fppf}$, and
\item if $F$ is an algebraic space over $S$, then $f^{-1}F$ is an algebraic
space over $S$ also.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Fully faithful
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04W1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 04W1}}



Suppose $\Sch_{fppf}$ is contained in $\Sch'_{fppf}$.
Let $S$ be an object of $\Sch_{fppf}$. Denote
$\textit{Spaces}/S$ the category of algebraic spaces over $S$
defined using $\Sch_{fppf}$. Similarly, denote
$\textit{Spaces}'/S$ the category of algebraic spaces over $S$
defined using $\Sch'_{fppf}$. The construction of
Lemma \ref{spaces-lemma-change-big-site}
defines a fully faithful functor
$$
\textit{Spaces}/S \longrightarrow \textit{Spaces}'/S
$$
whose essential image consists of those $X' \in \Ob(\textit{Spaces}'/S)$
such that there exist $U, R \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$\footnote{Requiring the
existence of $R$ is necessary because of our choice of the function $Bound$ in
Sets, Equation (\ref{sets-equation-bound}). The size of the fibre product
$U \times_{X'} U$ can grow faster than $Bound$ in terms of the size of $U$. We
can illustrate this by setting $S = \Spec(A)$, $U = \Spec(A[x_i, i \in I])$ and
$R = \coprod_{(\lambda_i) \in A^I} \Spec(A[x_i, y_i]/(x_i - \lambda_i y_i))$.
In this case the size of $R$ grows like $\kappa^\kappa$ where $\kappa$ is the
size of $U$.} and morphisms
$$
U \longrightarrow X'
\quad\text{and}\quad
R \longrightarrow U \times_{X'} U
$$
in $\Sh((\Sch'/S)_{fppf})$ which are surjective as maps of sheaves
(for example if the displayed morphisms are surjective and \'etale).

nodes.title: Change base scheme
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03I4}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03I4}}


Suppose given a big site $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $g : S \to S'$ be morphism of $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $j : (\Sch/S)_{fppf} \to (\Sch/S')_{fppf}$ be
the corresponding localization functor.
Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item for a scheme $T'$ over $S'$ we have
$j_!F(T'/S') =
\coprod\nolimits_{\varphi : T' \to S} F(T' \xrightarrow{\varphi} S),$
\item if $F$ is representable by a scheme
$X \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$,
then $j_!F$ is representable by $j(X)$ which is
$X$ viewed as a scheme over $S'$, and
\item if $F$ is an algebraic space over $S$, then $j_!F$ is an algebraic
space over $S'$, and if $F = U/R$ is a presentation, then
$j_!F = j(U)/j(R)$ is a presentation.
\end{enumerate}
Let $F'$ be a sheaf of sets on $(\Sch/S')_{fppf}$. Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(4)] for a scheme $T$ over $S$ we have $j^{-1}F'(T/S) = F'(T/S')$,
\item[(5)] if $F'$ is representable by a scheme
$X' \in \Ob((\Sch/S')_{fppf})$, then
$j^{-1}F'$ is representable, namely by $X'_S = S \times_{S'} X'$, and
\item[(6)] if $F'$ is an algebraic space, then
$j^{-1}F'$ is an algebraic space, and if $F' = U'/R'$ is a presentation,
then $j^{-1}F' = U'_S/R'_S$ is a presentation.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Base change
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03I5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03I5}}



Let $\Sch_{fppf}$ be a big fppf site.
Let $S \to S'$ be a morphism of this site.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $F'$ is an algebraic space over $S'$, then the
{\it base change of $F'$ to $S$} is the
algebraic space $j^{-1}F'$ described in
Lemma \ref{spaces-lemma-change-base-scheme}. We denote it $F'_S$.
\item If $F$ is an algebraic space over $S$, then $F$
{\it viewed as an algebraic space over $S'$}
is the algebraic space $j_!F$ over $S'$ described in
Lemma \ref{spaces-lemma-change-base-scheme}. We often simply denote this
$F$; if not then we will write $j_!F$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Category of spaces over smaller base scheme
Rephrase
Viewed as properties
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03I6}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03I6}}



Let $\Sch_{fppf}$ be a big fppf site.
Let $S \to S'$ be a morphism of this site.
Let $F$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $T$ be a scheme over $S$ and let $f : T \to F$ be
a morphism over $S$.
Let $f' : T' \to F'$ be the morphism over $S'$ we get from
$f$ by applying the equivalence of categories described in
Lemma \ref{spaces-lemma-category-of-spaces-over-smaller-base-scheme}.
For any property $\mathcal{P}$ as in
Definition \ref{spaces-definition-relative-representable-property}
we have $\mathcal{P}(f') \Leftrightarrow \mathcal{P}(f)$.

nodes.title: Quasi finite in codim 1
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AD1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AD1}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Assume $f$ is locally of finite type and $Y$ is locally Noetherian.
Let $y \in |Y|$ be a point of codimension $\leq 1$ on $Y$.
Let $X^0 \subset |X|$ be the set of points of codimension $0$ on $X$.
Assume in addition one of the following conditions is satisfied
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every $x \in X^0$ the transcendence degree of $x/f(x)$ is $0$,
\item for every $x \in X^0$ with $f(x) \leadsto y$
the transcendence degree of $x/f(x)$ is $0$,
\item $f$ is quasi-finite at every $x \in X^0$,
\item $f$ is quasi-finite at a dense set of points of $|X|$,
\item add more here.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ is quasi-finite at every point of $X$ lying over $y$.

nodes.title: Finite in codim 1
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AD2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AD2}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Assume $f$ is proper and $Y$ is locally Noetherian.
Let $y \in Y$ be a point of codimension $\leq 1$ in $Y$.
Let $X^0 \subset |X|$ be the set of points of codimension $0$ on $X$.
Assume in addition one of the
following conditions is satisfied
\begin{enumerate}
\item for every $x \in X^0$ the transcendence degree of $x/f(x)$ is $0$,
\item for every $x \in X^0$ with $f(x) \leadsto y$ the transcendence degree
of $x/f(x)$ is $0$,
\item $f$ is quasi-finite at every $x \in X^0$,
\item $f$ is quasi-finite at a dense set of points of $|X|$,
\item add more here.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists an open subspace $Y' \subset Y$ containing $y$ such that
$Y' \times_Y X \to Y'$ is finite.

nodes.title: Modification normal iso over codimension 1
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0BBQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0BBQ}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a Noetherian algebraic space over $S$.
Let $f : Y \to X$ be a birational proper morphism of algebraic spaces
with $Y$ reduced.
Let $U \subset X$ be the maximal open over which $f$ is an isomorphism.
Then $U$ contains
\begin{enumerate}
\item every point of codimension $0$ in $X$,
\item every $x \in |X|$ of codimension $1$ on $X$ such that the local ring of
$X$ at $x$ is normal (Properties of Spaces, Remark
\ref{spaces-properties-remark-list-properties-local-ring-local-etale-topology}),
and
\item every $x \in |X|$ such that the fibre of $|Y| \to |X|$ over $x$ is
finite and such that the local ring of $X$ at $x$ is normal.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Integral algebraic space
Integral algebraic space rational functions
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0END}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0END}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an integral algebraic space over $S$.
Let $\eta \in |X|$ be the generic point of $X$.
There are canonical identifications
$$
R(X) = \mathcal{O}_{X, \eta}^h = \kappa(\eta)
$$
where $R(X)$ is the ring of rational functions defined in
Morphisms of Spaces, Definition
\ref{spaces-morphisms-definition-ring-of-rational-functions},
$\kappa(\eta)$ is the residue field defined in
Decent Spaces, Definition \ref{decent-spaces-definition-residue-field},
and $\mathcal{O}_{X, \eta}^h$ is the henselian local ring defined in
Decent Spaces, Definition
\ref{decent-spaces-definition-elemenary-etale-neighbourhood}.
In particular, these rings are fields.

nodes.title: Function field
Integral sections
Normal integral cover by affines
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AYH}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AYH}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a normal integral algebraic space over $S$.
For every $x \in |X|$ there exists a normal integral affine scheme $U$
and an \'etale morphism $U \to X$ such that $x$ is in the image.

nodes.title: Normal integral sections
Decent irreducible closed
Finite degree
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AD5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AD5}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$, $Y$ be integral algebraic spaces over $S$
Let $x \in |X|$ and $y \in |Y|$ be the generic points. Let $f : X \to Y$
be locally of finite type. Assume $f$ is dominant
(Morphisms of Spaces, Definition \ref{spaces-morphisms-definition-dominant}).
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the transcendence degree of $x/y$ is $0$,
\item the extension $\kappa(x)/\kappa(y)$ (see proof) is finite,
\item there exist nonempty affine opens $U \subset X$ and $V \subset Y$
such that $f(U) \subset V$ and $f|_U : U \to V$ is finite,
\item $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$, and
\item $x$ is the only point of $|X|$ mapping to $y$.
\end{enumerate}
If $f$ is separated or if $f$ is quasi-compact, then these are
also equivalent to
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(6)] there exists a nonempty affine open $V \subset Y$ such
that $f^{-1}(V) \to V$ is finite.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Degree
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AD6}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AD6}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ and $Y$ be integral algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be locally of finite type and dominant.
Assume any of the equivalent conditions (1) -- (5) of
Lemma \ref{spaces-over-fields-lemma-finite-degree}. Let $x \in |X|$ and $y \in |Y|$
be the generic points. Then the positive integer
$$
\deg(X/Y) = [\kappa(x) : \kappa(y)]
$$
is called the {\it degree of $X$ over $Y$}.

nodes.title: Degree composition
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ENH}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0ENH}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$, $Y$, $Z$ be integral algebraic spaces over $S$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ and $g : Y \to Z$ be dominant morphisms locally
of finite type. Assume any of the equivalent conditions
(1) -- (5) of Lemma \ref{spaces-over-fields-lemma-finite-degree} hold for $f$ and $g$. Then
$$
\deg(X/Z) = \deg(X/Y) \deg(Y/Z).
$$

nodes.title: Components locally finite
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EE5}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EE5}}


Let $S$ be a scheme and let $X$ be a locally Noetherian
algebraic space over $S$. If $T \subset |X|$ is a closed subset,
then the collection of irreducible components of $T$ is locally finite.

nodes.title: Weil divisor
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ENJ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0ENJ}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item A {\it prime divisor} is an integral closed subspace $Z \subset X$
of codimension $1$, i.e., the generic point of $|Z|$ is a point
of codimension $1$ on $X$.
\item A {\it Weil divisor} is a formal sum $D = \sum n_Z Z$ where
the sum is over prime divisors of $X$ and the collection
$\{|Z| : n_Z \not = 0\}$ is locally finite in $|X|$
(Topology, Definition \ref{topology-definition-locally-finite}).
\end{enumerate}
The group of all Weil divisors on $X$ is denoted $\text{Div}(X)$.

nodes.title: Order vanishing
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ENK}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0ENK}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space
over $S$. Let $Z \subset X$ be a prime divisor and let $\xi \in |Z|$ be
the generic point. Then the henselian local ring $\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h$
is a reduced $1$-dimensional Noetherian local ring and
there is a canonical injective map
$$
R(X) \longrightarrow Q(\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h)
$$
from the function field $R(X)$ of $X$ into the total ring of fractions.

nodes.title: Order vanishing
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ENL}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0ENL}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic
space over $S$. Let $f \in R(X)^*$. For every prime divisor
$Z \subset X$ we define the {\it order of vanishing of $f$ along $Z$}
as the integer
$$
\text{ord}_Z(f) =
\text{length}_{\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h}
(\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h/a \mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h) -
\text{length}_{\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h}
(\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h/b \mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h)
$$
where $a, b \in \mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h$ are nonzerodivisors
such that the image of $f$ in $Q(\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h)$
(Lemma \ref{spaces-over-fields-lemma-order-vanishing}) is equal to $a/b$.
This is well defined by
Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-ord-additive}.

nodes.title: Order vanishing agrees
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ENM}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0ENM}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic
space over $S$. Let $f \in R(X)^*$. If the prime divisor
$Z \subset X$ meets the schematic locus of $X$, then the order
of vanishing $\text{ord}_Z(f)$ of Definition \ref{spaces-over-fields-definition-order-vanishing}
agrees with the order of vanishing of
Divisors, Definition \ref{divisors-definition-order-vanishing}.

nodes.title: Divisor locally finite
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ENN}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0ENN}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space
over $S$. Let $f \in R(X)^*$. Then the collections
$$
\{Z \subset X \mid Z\text{ a prime divisor with generic point }\xi
\text{ and }f\text{ not in }\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}\}
$$
and
$$
\{Z \subset X \mid Z \text{ a prime divisor and }\text{ord}_Z(f) \not = 0\}
$$
are locally finite in $X$.

nodes.title: Principal divisor
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ENP}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0ENP}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space over $S$.
Let $f \in R(X)^*$.
The {\it principal Weil divisor associated to $f$} is the Weil divisor
$$
\text{div}(f) = \text{div}_X(f) = \sum \text{ord}_Z(f) [Z]
$$
where the sum is over prime divisors and $\text{ord}_Z(f)$ is as in
Definition \ref{spaces-over-fields-definition-order-vanishing}. This makes sense
by Lemma \ref{spaces-over-fields-lemma-divisor-locally-finite}.

nodes.title: Div additive
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ENQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0ENQ}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space over $S$.
Let $f, g \in R(X)^*$. Then
$$
\text{div}_X(fg) = \text{div}_X(f) + \text{div}_X(g)
$$
as Weil divisors on $X$.

nodes.title: Class group
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ENR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0ENR}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space over $S$. The
{\it Weil divisor class group} of $X$ is the quotient of
the group of Weil divisors by the subgroup of principal Weil divisors.
Notation: $\text{Cl}(X)$.

nodes.title: Order vanishing meromorphic
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EPR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EPR}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral
algebraic algebraic space over $S$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an
invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in \Gamma(X, \mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{L}))$
be a regular meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L}$.
For every prime divisor $Z \subset X$ with generic point $\xi \in |Z|$
we define the
{\it order of vanishing of $s$ along $Z$}
as the integer
$$
\text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s) =
\text{length}_{\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h}
(\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h/a \mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h) -
\text{length}_{\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h}
(\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h/b \mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h)
$$
where $a, b \in \mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h$ are nonzerodivisors
such that the element $s/s_\xi$ of $Q(\mathcal{O}_{X, \xi}^h)$
constructed above is equal to $a/b$.
This is well defined by the above and
Algebra, Lemma \ref{algebra-lemma-ord-additive}.

nodes.title: Divisor meromorphic locally finite
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EPS}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EPS}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space
over $S$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s \in \mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{L})$ be a
regular (i.e., nonzero) meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L}$. Then the sets
$$
\{Z \subset X \mid Z \text{ a prime divisor with generic point }\xi
\text{ and }s\text{ not in }\mathcal{L}_\xi\}
$$
and
$$
\{Z \subset X \mid Z \text{ is a prime divisor and }
\text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s) \not = 0\}
$$
are locally finite in $X$.

nodes.title: Divisor meromorphic well defined
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EPT}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EPT}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space
over $S$ Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
Let $s, s' \in \mathcal{K}_X(\mathcal{L})$ be nonzero
meromorphic sections of $\mathcal{L}$. Then $f = s/s'$
is an element of $R(X)^*$ and we have
$$
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s)[Z]
=
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s')[Z]
+
\text{div}(f)
$$
as Weil divisors.

nodes.title: Divisor invertible sheaf
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EPU}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EPU}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space
over $S$. Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
\begin{enumerate}
\item For any nonzero meromorphic section $s$ of $\mathcal{L}$
we define the {\it Weil divisor associated to $s$} as
$$
\text{div}_\mathcal{L}(s) =
\sum \text{ord}_{Z, \mathcal{L}}(s) [Z] \in \text{Div}(X)
$$
where the sum is over prime divisors. This is well defined by
Lemma \ref{spaces-over-fields-lemma-divisor-meromorphic-locally-finite}.
\item We define {\it Weil divisor class associated to $\mathcal{L}$}
as the image of $\text{div}_\mathcal{L}(s)$ in $\text{Cl}(X)$
where $s$ is any nonzero meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L}$ over $X$.
This is well defined by
Lemma \ref{spaces-over-fields-lemma-divisor-meromorphic-well-defined}.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: C1 additive
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EPV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EPV}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space
over $S$. Let $\mathcal{L}$, $\mathcal{N}$ be invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Let $s$, resp.\ $t$ be a nonzero meromorphic section
of $\mathcal{L}$, resp.\ $\mathcal{N}$. Then $st$ is a nonzero
meromorphic section of $\mathcal{L} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{N}$ and
$$
\text{div}_{\mathcal{L} \otimes \mathcal{N}}(st)
=
\text{div}_\mathcal{L}(s) + \text{div}_\mathcal{N}(t)
$$
in $\text{Div}(X)$. In particular, the Weil divisor class of
$\mathcal{L} \otimes_{\mathcal{O}_X} \mathcal{N}$ is the sum
of the Weil divisor classes of $\mathcal{L}$ and $\mathcal{N}$.

nodes.title: Normal c1 injective
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EPX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EPX}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be a locally Noetherian integral algebraic space
over $S$. If $X$ is normal, then the map (\ref{equation-c1})
$\Pic(X) \to \text{Cl}(X)$ is injective.

nodes.title: Modification
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AD8}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AD8}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an integral algebraic space over $S$. A
{\it modification of $X$} is a birational proper morphism
$f : X' \to X$ of algebraic spaces over $S$ with $X'$ integral.

nodes.title: Modification iso over open
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AD9}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AD9}}


Let $f : X' \to X$ be a modification as in
Definition \ref{spaces-over-fields-definition-modification}.
There exists a nonempty open $U \subset X$ such that $f^{-1}(U) \to U$
is an isomorphism.

nodes.title: Alteration
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ADA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0ADA}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an integral algebraic space over $S$.
An {\it alteration of $X$} is a proper dominant morphism $f : Y \to X$
of algebraic spaces over $S$ with $Y$ integral such that $f^{-1}(U) \to U$
is finite for some nonempty open $U \subset X$.

nodes.title: Alteration generically finite
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ADB}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0ADB}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper dominant morphism of
integral algebraic spaces over $S$. Then $f$ is an alteration
if and only if any of the equivalent conditions (1) -- (6) of
Lemma \ref{spaces-over-fields-lemma-finite-degree} hold.

nodes.title: Alteration contained in
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DMN}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DMN}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a proper surjective morphism of
algebraic spaces over $S$. Assume $Y$ is integral. Then
there exists an integral closed subspace $X' \subset X$ such that
$f' = f|_{X'} : X' \to Y$ is an alteration.

nodes.title: Locally finite type dim zero
Generic point in schematic locus
Separated algebraic spaces are schemes in codimension 1.
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0ADD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0ADD}}



Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $S$.
Let $x \in |X|$. If $X$ is separated, locally Noetherian, and
the dimension of the local ring of $X$ at $x$ is $\leq 1$
(Properties of Spaces, Definition
\ref{spaces-properties-definition-dimension-local-ring}),
then there exists an open subspace of $X$ containing $x$ which is a scheme.

nodes.title: Scheme after purely inseparable base change
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B83}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0B83}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $k$.
If there exists a purely inseparable field extension $k'/k$
such that $X_{k'}$ is a scheme, then $X$ is a scheme.

nodes.title: When scheme after base change
Base change by Galois
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B86}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0B86}}


Let $k'/k$ be a finite Galois extension with Galois group $G$.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $k$. Then $G$ acts freely on the
algebraic space $X_{k'}$ and $X = X_{k'}/G$ in the sense of
Properties of Spaces, Lemma \ref{spaces-properties-lemma-quotient}.

nodes.title: When quotient scheme at point
Scheme after purely transcendental base change
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0B85}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0B85}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a quasi-separated
algebraic space over $k$. If there exists a purely transcendental
field extension $K/k$ such that $X_K$ is a scheme, then
$X$ is a scheme.

nodes.title: Scheme over algebraic closure enough affines
Locally quasi finite over field
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06S0}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06S0}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $k$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is locally quasi-finite over $k$,
\item $X$ is locally of finite type over $k$ and has dimension $0$,
\item $X$ is a scheme and is locally quasi-finite over $k$,
\item $X$ is a scheme and is locally of finite type over $k$ and has
dimension $0$, and
\item $X$ is a disjoint union of spectra of Artinian local $k$-algebras
$A$ over $k$ with $\dim_k(A) < \infty$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Mono towards locally quasi finite over field
Geometrically reduced
Geometrically reduced at point
Geometrically reduced
Perfect reduced
Geometrically reduced positive characteristic
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E03}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0E03}}


Let $k$ be a field of characteristic $p > 0$. Let $X$ be an algebraic space
over $k$. The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is geometrically reduced over $k$,
\item $X_{k'}$ is reduced for every field extension $k'/k$,
\item $X_{k'}$ is reduced for every
finite purely inseparable field extension $k'/k$,
\item $X_{k^{1/p}}$ is reduced,
\item $X_{k^{perf}}$ is reduced, and
\item $X_{\bar k}$ is reduced.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Geometrically reduced upstairs
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E04}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0E04}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $k$.
Let $k'/k$ be a field extension. Let $x \in |X|$ be a point and let
$x' \in |X_{k'}|$ be a point lying over $x$.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $X$ is geometrically reduced at $x$,
\item $X_{k'}$ is geometrically reduced at $x'$.
\end{enumerate}
In particular, $X$ is geometrically reduced over $k$ if and only if
$X_{k'}$ is geometrically reduced over $k'$.

nodes.title: Geometrically reduced etale local
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0E05}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0E05}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of
algebraic spaces over $k$. Let $x \in |X|$ be a point
with image $y \in |Y|$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item if $f$ is \'etale at $x$, then
$X$ is geometrically reduced at $x$ $\Leftrightarrow$
$Y$ is geometrically reduced at $y$,
\item if $f$ is surjective \'etale, then
$X$ is geometrically reduced $\Leftrightarrow$
$Y$ is geometrically reduced.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Geometrically connected
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A0Z}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0A0Z}}


Let $X$ be an algebraic space over the field $k$. We say $X$ is
{\it geometrically connected} over $k$ if the base change $X_{k'}$
is connected for every field extension $k'$ of $k$.

nodes.title: Geometrically connected check after extension
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A10}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0A10}}


Let $X$ be an algebraic space over the field $k$.
Let $k'/k$ be a field extension.
Then $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$ if and only if
$X_{k'}$ is geometrically connected over $k'$.

nodes.title: Bijection connected components
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A11}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0A11}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$, $Y$ be algebraic spaces over $k$.
Assume $X$ is geometrically connected over $k$.
Then the projection morphism
$$
p : X \times_k Y \longrightarrow Y
$$
induces a bijection between connected components.

nodes.title: Separably closed field connected components
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A12}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0A12}}


Let $k'/k$ be an extension of fields. Let $X$ be an algebraic space
over $k$. Assume $k$ separably algebraically closed. Then the morphism
$X_{k'} \to X$ induces a bijection of connected components. In particular,
$X$ is geometrically connected over $k$ if and only if $X$ is connected.

nodes.title: Characterize geometrically connected
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A13}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0A13}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $k$.
Let $\overline{k}$ be a separable algebraic closure of $k$.
Then $X$ is geometrically connected if and only if the base change
$X_{\overline{k}}$ is connected.

nodes.title: Galois action quasi compact open
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A15}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0A15}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $k$.
Let $\overline{k}$ be a (possibly infinite) Galois extension of $k$.
Let $V \subset X_{\overline{k}}$ be a quasi-compact open.
Then
\begin{enumerate}
\item there exists a finite subextension $\overline{k}/k'/k$
and a quasi-compact open $V' \subset X_{k'}$ such that
$V = (V')_{\overline{k}}$,
\item there exists an open subgroup $H \subset \text{Gal}(\overline{k}/k)$
such that $\sigma(V) = V$ for all $\sigma \in H$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Closed fixed by Galois
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0A16}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0A16}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $\overline{k}/k$ be a (possibly infinite)
Galois extension. Let $X$ be an algebraic space over $k$. Let
$\overline{T} \subset |X_{\overline{k}}|$ have the following properties
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\overline{T}$ is a closed subset of $|X_{\overline{k}}|$,
\item for every $\sigma \in \text{Gal}(\overline{k}/k)$
we have $\sigma(\overline{T}) = \overline{T}$.
\end{enumerate}
Then there exists a closed subset $T \subset |X|$ whose inverse image
in $|X_{k'}|$ is $\overline{T}$.

nodes.title: Characterize geometrically disconnected
Geometrically irreducible
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DMU}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DMU}}


Let $k$ be a field.
Let $X$ be a decent algebraic space over $k$.
We say $X$ is {\it geometrically irreducible} if the
topological space $|X_{k'}|$ is
irreducible\footnote{An irreducible space is nonempty.}
for any field extension $k'$ of $k$.

nodes.title: Geometrically integral
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DMW}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DMW}}


Let $X$ be an algebraic space over the field $k$. We say $X$ is
{\it geometrically integral} over $k$ if the algebraic space
$X_{k'}$ is integral (Definition \ref{spaces-over-fields-definition-integral-algebraic-space})
for every field extension $k'$ of $k$.

nodes.title: Geometrically integral
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DMX}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DMX}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a decent algebraic space over $k$.
Then $X$ is geometrically integral over $k$ if and only if
$X$ is both geometrically reduced and geometrically irreducible
over $k$.

nodes.title: Proper geometrically reduced global sections
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DMY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DMY}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper algebraic space over $k$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item $A = H^0(X, \mathcal{O}_X)$ is a finite dimensional $k$-algebra,
\item $A = \prod_{i = 1, \ldots, n} A_i$ is a product of Artinian
local $k$-algebras, one factor for each connected component of $|X|$,
\item if $X$ is reduced, then $A = \prod_{i = 1, \ldots, n} k_i$
is a product of fields, each a finite extension of $k$,
\item if $X$ is geometrically reduced, then $k_i$ is finite separable
over $k$,
\item if $X$ is geometrically connected, then $A$ is geometrically
irreducible over $k$,
\item if $X$ is geometrically irreducible, then $A$ is geometrically
irreducible over $k$,
\item if $X$ is geometrically reduced and connected, then $A = k$, and
\item if $X$ is geometrically integral, then $A = k$.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: Characterize trivial pic integral
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DMZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DMZ}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper integral algebraic space over $k$.
Let $\mathcal{L}$ be an invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-module.
If $H^0(X, \mathcal{L})$ and $H^0(X, \mathcal{L}^{\otimes - 1})$
are both nonzero, then $\mathcal{L} \cong \mathcal{O}_X$.

nodes.title: Integral dimension
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EDB}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EDB}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be an integral morphism
of algebraic spaces. Then $\dim(X) \leq \dim(Y)$.
If $f$ is surjective then $\dim(X) = \dim(Y)$.

nodes.title: Alteration dimension
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EDC}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EDC}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $Y$ is locally Noetherian,
\item $X$ and $Y$ are integral algebraic spaces,
\item $f$ is dominant, and
\item $f$ is locally of finite type.
\end{enumerate}
If $x \in |X|$ and $y \in |Y|$ are the generic points, then
$$
\dim(X) \leq \dim(Y) + \text{transcendence degree of }x/y.
$$
If $f$ is proper, then equality holds.

nodes.title: Smooth regular
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/06M1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 06M1}}


Let $k$ be a field.
Let $X$ be an algebraic space smooth over $k$.
Then $X$ is a regular algebraic space.

nodes.title: Smooth separable closed points dense
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/07W4}{\texttt{Stacks tag 07W4}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be an algebraic space smooth over $\Spec(k)$.
The set of $x \in |X|$ which are image of morphisms $\Spec(k') \to X$
with $k' \supset k$ finite separable is dense in $|X|$.

nodes.title: Euler characteristic
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DN1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DN1}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper algebraic over $k$. Let $\mathcal{F}$
be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. In this situation the
{\it Euler characteristic of $\mathcal{F}$} is the integer
$$
\chi(X, \mathcal{F}) = \sum\nolimits_i (-1)^i \dim_k H^i(X, \mathcal{F}).
$$
For justification of the formula see below.

nodes.title: Euler characteristic additive
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DN2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DN2}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper algebraic space over $k$.
Let $0 \to \mathcal{F}_1 \to \mathcal{F}_2 \to \mathcal{F}_3 \to 0$
be a short exact sequence of coherent modules on $X$. Then
$$
\chi(X, \mathcal{F}_2) = \chi(X, \mathcal{F}_1) + \chi(X, \mathcal{F}_3)
$$

nodes.title: Euler characteristic morphism
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EDD}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EDD}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a morphism of
algebraic spaces proper over $k$. Let $\mathcal{G}$ be a
coherent $\mathcal{O}_Y$-module. Then
$$
\chi(Y, \mathcal{G}) = \sum (-1)^i \chi(X, R^if_*\mathcal{G})
$$

nodes.title: Numerical polynomial from euler
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0DN4}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0DN4}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper algebraic space over $k$.
Let $\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let
$\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_r$ be invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
The map
$$
(n_1, \ldots, n_r) \longmapsto
\chi(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes
\mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1} \otimes \ldots \otimes
\mathcal{L}_r^{\otimes n_r})
$$
is a numerical polynomial in $n_1, \ldots, n_r$ of total degree at
most the dimension of the scheme theoretic support of $\mathcal{F}$.

nodes.title: Numerical polynomial leading term
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EDE}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EDE}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper algebraic space over $k$. Let
$\mathcal{F}$ be a coherent $\mathcal{O}_X$-module. Let
$\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_r$ be invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Let $d = \dim(\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F}))$.
Let $Z_i \subset X$ be the irreducible components
of $\text{Supp}(\mathcal{F})$ of dimension $d$. Let $\overline{x}_i$
be a geometric generic point of $Z_i$ and set
$m_i = \text{length}_{\mathcal{O}_{X, \overline{x}_i}}
(\mathcal{F}_{\overline{x}_i})$.
Then
$$
\chi(X, \mathcal{F} \otimes \mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1} \otimes \ldots \otimes
\mathcal{L}_r^{\otimes n_r}) -
\sum\nolimits_i
m_i\ \chi(Z_i, \mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1} \otimes \ldots \otimes
\mathcal{L}_r^{\otimes n_r}|_{Z_i})
$$
is a numerical polynomial in $n_1, \ldots, n_r$ of total degree $< d$.

nodes.title: Intersection number
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EDF}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EDF}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper algebraic space over $k$. Let
$i : Z \to X$ be a closed subspace of dimension $d$. Let
$\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_d$ be invertible
$\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. We define the {\it intersection number}
$(\mathcal{L}_1 \cdots \mathcal{L}_d \cdot Z)$
as the coefficient of $n_1 \ldots n_d$ in the numerical polynomial
$$
\chi(X, i_*\mathcal{O}_Z \otimes \mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1} \otimes
\ldots \otimes \mathcal{L}_d^{\otimes n_d}) =
\chi(Z, \mathcal{L}_1^{\otimes n_1} \otimes
\ldots \otimes \mathcal{L}_d^{\otimes n_d}|_Z)
$$
In the special
case that $\mathcal{L}_1 = \ldots = \mathcal{L}_d = \mathcal{L}$
we write $(\mathcal{L}^d \cdot Z)$.

nodes.title: Intersection number integer
Intersection number additive
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EDH}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EDH}}


In the situation of Definition \ref{spaces-over-fields-definition-intersection-number}
the intersection number
$(\mathcal{L}_1 \cdots \mathcal{L}_d \cdot Z)$
is additive: if $\mathcal{L}_i = \mathcal{L}_i' \otimes \mathcal{L}_i''$,
then we have
$$
(\mathcal{L}_1 \cdots \mathcal{L}_i \cdots \mathcal{L}_d \cdot Z) =
(\mathcal{L}_1 \cdots \mathcal{L}_i' \cdots \mathcal{L}_d \cdot Z) +
(\mathcal{L}_1 \cdots \mathcal{L}_i'' \cdots \mathcal{L}_d \cdot Z)
$$

nodes.title: Intersection number in terms of components
Intersection number and pullback
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EDJ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EDJ}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $f : Y \to X$ be a morphism of
algebraic spaces proper over $k$.
Let $Z \subset Y$ be an integral closed subspace of dimension $d$ and let
$\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_d$ be invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules.
Then
$$
(f^*\mathcal{L}_1 \cdots f^*\mathcal{L}_d \cdot Z) =
\deg(f|_Z : Z \to f(Z)) (\mathcal{L}_1 \cdots \mathcal{L}_d \cdot f(Z))
$$
where $\deg(Z \to f(Z))$ is as in Definition \ref{spaces-over-fields-definition-degree}
or $0$ if $\dim(f(Z)) < d$.

nodes.title: Numerical intersection effective Cartier divisor
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0EDK}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0EDK}}


Let $k$ be a field. Let $X$ be a proper algebraic space over $k$.
Let $Z \subset X$ be a closed subspace of dimension $d$.
Let $\mathcal{L}_1, \ldots, \mathcal{L}_d$
be invertible $\mathcal{O}_X$-modules. Assume there exists an
effective Cartier divisor $D \subset Z$ such that
$\mathcal{L}_1|_Z \cong \mathcal{O}_Z(D)$. Then
$$
(\mathcal{L}_1 \cdots \mathcal{L}_d \cdot Z) =
(\mathcal{L}_2 \cdots \mathcal{L}_d \cdot D)
$$

nodes.title: Morphism representable by spaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YQ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02YQ}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$, $G$ be presheaves on $\Sch_{fppf}/S$.
We say a morphism $a : F \to G$ is
{\it representable by algebraic spaces}
if for every $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$ and
any $\xi : U \to G$ the fiber product $U \times_{\xi, G} F$
is an algebraic space.

nodes.title: Morphism spaces is representable by spaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03BN}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03BN}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Then $f$ is representable by algebraic spaces.

nodes.title: A base change of a representable by algebraic spaces morphism of presheaves is represen...
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03Y0}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03Y0}}



Let $S$ be a scheme. Let
$$
\begin{array}{cc}G' \times_G F \longrightarrow\overset{a'}{\downarrow} & F \overset{a}{\downarrow} \\ G' \longrightarrow & G\end{array}
$$
be a fibre square of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
If $a$ is representable by algebraic spaces so is $a'$.

nodes.title: Representable by spaces transformation to sheaf
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YR}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02YR}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $a : F \to G$ be representable by algebraic spaces.
If $G$ is a sheaf, then so is $F$.

nodes.title: Representable by spaces transformation diagonal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/05LA}{\texttt{Stacks tag 05LA}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $a : F \to G$ be representable by algebraic spaces.
Then $\Delta_{F/G} : F \to F \times_G F$ is representable by
algebraic spaces.

nodes.title: Representable by spaces over space
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/02YS}{\texttt{Stacks tag 02YS}}


Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $a : F \to G$ be representable by algebraic spaces.
If $G$ is an algebraic space, then so is $F$.

nodes.title: Representable by spaces
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03XY}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03XY}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $a : F \to G$ be a map of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
Suppose $a : F \to G$ is representable by algebraic spaces.
If $X$ is an algebraic space over $S$, and $X \to G$ is a map of presheaves
then $X \times_G F$ is an algebraic space.

nodes.title: Composition transformation
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03Y1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03Y1}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}F \overset{a}{\longrightarrow} & G \overset{b}{\longrightarrow} & H\end{array}
$$
be maps of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
If $a$ and $b$ are representable by algebraic spaces, so is
$b \circ a$.

nodes.title: Product transformations
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/046D}{\texttt{Stacks tag 046D}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F_i, G_i : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$, $i = 1, 2$.
Let $a_i : F_i \to G_i$, $i = 1, 2$
be representable by algebraic spaces.
Then
$$
a_1 \times a_2 : F_1 \times F_2 \longrightarrow G_1 \times G_2
$$
is a representable by algebraic spaces.

nodes.title: Representable by spaces permanence
Glueing sheaves
Property transformation
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03XZ}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03XZ}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $a : F \to G$ be a map of presheaves on
$(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$ which is representable by algebraic spaces.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property of morphisms of algebraic spaces which
\begin{enumerate}
\item is preserved under any base change, and
\item is fppf local on the base, see
Descent on Spaces,
Definition \ref{spaces-descent-definition-property-morphisms-local}.
\end{enumerate}
In this case we say that $a$ has {\it property $\mathcal{P}$} if for every
scheme $U$ and $\xi : U \to G$ the resulting morphism of algebraic spaces
$U \times_G F \to U$ has property $\mathcal{P}$.

nodes.title: Base change transformation property
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/046F}{\texttt{Stacks tag 046F}}



Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property as in
Definition \ref{bootstrap-definition-property-transformation}.
Let
$$
\begin{array}{cc}G' \times_G F \longrightarrow\overset{a'}{\downarrow} & F \overset{a}{\downarrow} \\ G' \longrightarrow & G\end{array}
$$
be a fibre square of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
If $a$ is representable by algebraic spaces and has $\mathcal{P}$
so does $a'$.

nodes.title: Composition transformation property
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/046G}{\texttt{Stacks tag 046G}}



Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property as in
Definition \ref{bootstrap-definition-property-transformation},
and assume $\mathcal{P}$ is stable under composition.
Let
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}F \overset{a}{\longrightarrow} & G \overset{b}{\longrightarrow} & H\end{array}
$$
be maps of presheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
If $a$, $b$ are representable by algebraic spaces and has
$\mathcal{P}$ so does $b \circ a$.

nodes.title: Product transformations property
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/046H}{\texttt{Stacks tag 046H}}



Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F_i, G_i : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$,
$i = 1, 2$.
Let $a_i : F_i \to G_i$, $i = 1, 2$ be representable by algebraic spaces.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be a property as in
Definition \ref{bootstrap-definition-property-transformation}
which is stable under composition.
If $a_1$ and $a_2$ have property $\mathcal{P}$ so does
$a_1 \times a_2 : F_1 \times F_2 \longrightarrow G_1 \times G_2$.

nodes.title: Transformations property implication
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AM1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AM1}}



Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$.
Let $a : F \to G$ be a transformation of functors representable by
algebraic spaces.
Let $\mathcal{P}$, $\mathcal{P}'$ be properties as in
Definition \ref{bootstrap-definition-property-transformation}.
Suppose that for any morphism $f : X \to Y$ of algebraic spaces over $S$
we have $\mathcal{P}(f) \Rightarrow \mathcal{P}'(f)$.
If $a$ has property $\mathcal{P}$, then
$a$ has property $\mathcal{P}'$.

nodes.title: Surjective flat locally finite presentation
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/04S1}{\texttt{Stacks tag 04S1}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F, G : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be sheaves.
Let $a : F \to G$ be representable by algebraic spaces, flat,
locally of finite presentation, and surjective.
Then $a : F \to G$ is surjective as a map of sheaves.

nodes.title: The diagonal of a presheaf is representable by algebraic spaces if and only if every ma...
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03Y2}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03Y2}}



Let $S$ be a scheme.
If $F$ is a presheaf on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item $\Delta_F : F \to F \times F$ is representable by algebraic spaces,
\item for every scheme $T$ any map $T \to F$ is representable by algebraic
spaces, and
\item for every algebraic space $X$ any map $X \to F$ is representable
by algebraic spaces.
\end{enumerate}

nodes.title: After fppf sep lqf
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/046J}{\texttt{Stacks tag 046J}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let
$$
\begin{array}{cc}E \underset{a}{\longrightarrow}\underset{f}{\downarrow} & F \overset{g}{\downarrow} \\ H \overset{b}{\longrightarrow} & G\end{array}
$$
be a cartesian diagram of sheaves on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$, so
$E = H \times_G F$. If
\begin{enumerate}
\item $g$ is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat, and
locally of finite presentation, and
\item $a$ is representable by algebraic spaces, separated, and
locally quasi-finite
\end{enumerate}
then $b$ is representable (by schemes) as well as separated and
locally quasi-finite.

nodes.title: Bootstrap diagonal
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/046K}{\texttt{Stacks tag 046K}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the presheaf $F$ is a sheaf,
\item there exists an algebraic space $X$ and a map $X \to F$
which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, flat and
locally of finite presentation.
\end{enumerate}
Then $\Delta_F$ is representable (by schemes).

nodes.title: Bootstrap locally quasi finite
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AHV}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0AHV}}


Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $F : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a
functor. Let $X$ be a scheme and let $X \to F$ be representable by algebraic
spaces and locally quasi-finite. Then $X \to F$ is representable
(by schemes).

nodes.title: Bootstrap
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/03Y3}{\texttt{Stacks tag 03Y3}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $F : (\Sch/S)_{fppf}^{opp} \to \textit{Sets}$ be a functor.
Assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item the presheaf $F$ is a sheaf,
\item the diagonal morphism $F  \to F \times F$ is representable by
algebraic spaces, and
\item there exists an algebraic space $X$
and a map $X \to F$ which is surjective, and \'etale.
\end{enumerate}
or assume that
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] the presheaf $F$ is a sheaf, and
\item[(b)] there exists an algebraic space $X$ and a map $X \to F$
which is representable by algebraic spaces, surjective, and \'etale.
\end{enumerate}
Then $F$ is an algebraic space.

nodes.title: Better finding opens
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/046M}{\texttt{Stacks tag 046M}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $(U, R, s, t, c)$ be a groupoid scheme over $S$.
Let $g : U' \to U$ be a morphism.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item the composition
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}U' \times_{g, U, t} R \underset{\text{pr}_1}{\longrightarrow}\overset{h}{\longrightarrow} & R \underset{s}{\longrightarrow} & U\end{array}
$$
has an open image $W \subset U$, and
\item the resulting map $h : U' \times_{g, U, t} R \to W$
defines a surjection of sheaves in the fppf topology.
\end{enumerate}
Let $R' = R|_{U'}$ be the restriction of $R$ to $U'$. Then the map
of quotient sheaves
$$
U'/R' \to U/R
$$
in the fppf topology is representable, and is an open immersion.

nodes.title: Slice equivalence relation
nodes.statement:
\href{https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0489}{\texttt{Stacks tag 0489}}


Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $j : R \to U \times_S U$ be an equivalence relation on schemes over $S$.
Assume $s, t : R \to U$ are flat and locally of finite presentation.
Then there exists an equivalence relation $j' : R' \to U'\times_S U'$
on schemes over $S$, and an isomorphism
$$
U'/R' \longrightarrow U/R
$$
induced by a morphism $U' \to U$ which maps $R'$ into $R$ such that
$s', t' : R \to U$ are flat, locally of finite presentation
